data.name: Infinitrap Classic: Ohio Jack and The Cup Of Eternity
data.detailed_description:
InfiniTrap Classic is a fast paced puzzle game for hardcore players. The game contains 40 levels and is available on Windows, OSX and Linux.

Every level starts with the player character standing on the start tile. The start tile is perfectly safe-- No, trust me. It's safe. Once you leave the start tile, you have a limited time to reach the treasure before the level crushes you. To complicate things, each level will include a number of obstacles to waste your time and possibly kill you. You can make your own levels!

FEATURES


  • 40 challenging levels.
  • Blood and gore can be disabled.
  • Full gamepad support.
  • A full-featured level editor.
  • Custom levels support.
  • Supported languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, Portuguese

reviews.review:
Infinitrap Classic: Ohio Jack and The Cup Of Eternity is a fast-paced puzzle game that turns a seemingly simple treasure hunt into a relentless series of deadly obstacle courses. Developed and published by Shadebob Games, it places players in control of Ohio Jack as he searches for treasure while navigating environments packed with traps. The concept is immediately understandable, but surviving each stage requires considerably more than simply finding the exit. Timing, observation, route memorization, quick reactions, and a willingness to learn from repeated failures form the foundation of the experience.

The campaign contains 40 levels, with each one essentially functioning as a compact survival puzzle. Ohio Jack begins from a safe position, but once he moves away from it, the real challenge starts. Players have limited time to reach the treasure before the stage becomes fatal, preventing them from casually examining every corner at their leisure. This creates an effective sense of urgency because standing around trying to determine the safest route can be just as dangerous as recklessly charging ahead. Successful runs require a balance between speed and careful movement.

Death is an important part of the learning process. Traps can catch newcomers by surprise, and the first attempt at a level often becomes an opportunity to discover where its dangers are located. Subsequent attempts allow players to remember those hazards, adjust their route, and gradually improve their execution. The resulting trial-and-error structure can be satisfying because difficult stages become noticeably easier as their layouts are committed to memory. Clearing a level after several unsuccessful attempts produces a genuine feeling of accomplishment. At the same time, players who dislike repetition or unexpected deaths may find this design frustrating.

The traps themselves provide much of the game's entertainment. Hazards are designed to punish careless movement, while the timer discourages excessive caution. This creates a constant push-and-pull between moving quickly and anticipating what might happen next. The mechanics are straightforward enough to understand almost immediately, allowing the difficulty to come primarily from level design rather than complicated controls. It feels closer to an arcade challenge blended with puzzle solving than a traditional adventure game, making it particularly suitable for short sessions where players can repeatedly tackle troublesome stages.

Its presentation embraces a humorous and deliberately exaggerated personality. The colorful, cartoon-like appearance contrasts with the rather gruesome ways Ohio Jack can meet his end. Blood and gore add dark comedy to failed attempts instead of turning the game into serious horror. Players who prefer a cleaner presentation can disable the violent effects, which is a welcome option. The visuals are functional rather than technically impressive, but they fit the straightforward arcade nature of the experience and generally keep important hazards readable.

Replay value receives a substantial boost from the included level editor and support for custom stages. Players who finish the main campaign can experiment with designing their own trap-filled challenges or explore creations made by others. This is particularly well suited to the game's mechanics because even relatively small environments can become complicated puzzles when traps, timing, and route planning are combined effectively. Steam Workshop integration expands this community-oriented side of the game, while achievements, leaderboards, statistics, trading cards, and Steam Cloud functionality provide additional features for players interested in completion or competitive performance.

Full controller support is another useful addition, especially for gameplay that depends heavily on accurate movement and rapid reactions. The PC hardware requirements are extremely modest, so the game should be approachable even on older or lower-powered computers. Its small installation footprint also makes it convenient to keep installed for occasional sessions. Multiple operating systems and several interface languages further broaden accessibility without complicating the fundamental experience.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable advantage. The game is officially Steam Deck Verified, with its core functionality working through the handheld's controls and its interface remaining usable on the smaller display. Controller prompts and general navigation are appropriately supported, while the game can run using settings suitable for the device. Its viewpoint and methodical pacing also translate naturally to portable play, although demanding visual settings can still make sensible performance adjustments worthwhile for players prioritizing battery life or consistent performance.

Infinitrap Classic ultimately succeeds because it stays committed to a focused idea. It does not attempt to build an enormous adventure around Ohio Jack's treasure hunt. Instead, it concentrates on compact levels, lethal surprises, strict timing, repeated attempts, and the satisfaction of eventually mastering a difficult route. The 40-stage campaign provides the core challenge, while the editor and custom content give dedicated players reasons to continue beyond it. Its reliance on trial and error will naturally divide audiences, but anyone who enjoys difficult puzzle-action games where failure gradually teaches the solution should find plenty to appreciate. As a free-to-play experience, it offers a surprisingly complete package with enough personality and challenge to stand apart from more conventional puzzle games.

Rating: 7/10
